input.summary: Fail. The strict checker fails T-L1 for T2 with "0/2 ends loop" at (306,0). The new ring closes on itself at Harbour Road. N-D1 accepts it as a closed path, but T-L1 still treats (306,0) as two open ends with no turning loop. Datum's note claims the ring needs no loop; the checker contradicts that. Every other rule passes, including N-R1, which was last round's fault (worst plot now 194 m). The other blocker from last round is fixed: Skyport moved to x 545, so Harbour–Skyport is 205 m. Vantage moved Datum's T2 stop positions because Datum's pairs were 240 m and 260 m apart, under the tram minimum of 300 m. Vantage reported this honestly as done:false. Code raises that as a hand-off fault, so I do not repeat it. Open questions, not faults: no standard covers the flat T1×T2 crossing at (0,-726) (Keel/Splice to rule). Notes › why contradicts notes › concept (for Aster). The timetable choices are plausible: 8 m/s street trams with 15 s dwells, the sky rail at 12 m/s every 120 s, and journeys that cover all three interchanges. Pulse's open questions are about things the GDD has not decided (how the wait is computed, walking pace, closures, which way round the ring) and do not contradict the travel rule. Pulse's note that the ring is "about 2.9 km" understates it; Vantage measured 3242 m. This is minor and does not change the timetable choices.

faults.fault: T2 Ring Line fails T-L1 (0/2 ends loop, no loop at (306,0)). The ring is drawn as one running path whose first and last points are both (306,0), and the checker reads that as two open ends with no turning loop for single-ended trams. Datum's note says that because the ring closes on itself, N-D1 and T-L1 need no loop. N-D1 passes, but T-L1 does not.
faults.fix: Datum: model T2 in a form T-L1 accepts as closed, or add a terminal loop (R ≥ 25) in street space at the end. If a closed running ring should pass T-L1 by design, hand that to Splice through Aster to change the checker rule. Do not assume it passes. Then rerun `bun tools/plan/cli.ts` strict.
